newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria gives university lecturers ultimatum.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria gives university lecturers ultimatum.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has given striking university lecturers seven days to return to work or leave the campuses, an official statement said on Thursday.
The statement from the ministry of education said universities controlled by the banned Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) risked permanent closure.
ASUU, and two other academic unions were last month banned by the government after being on indefinite strike since April for better working conditions.
The strike has left tens of thousands of students idle at Nigeria's 38 universities.
ASUU president Asisi Asobie on Wednesday alleged a government plot to arrest lecturers who refused to return to work, and said it would only make matters worse.
According to Asobie, Nigerian lecturers earn about 3,000 naira ($35.29) monthly, much less than their counterparts in other African countries.
